accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Administrative Reforms Commission:
1. It submitted 15 reports.
2. Its reports were submitted during 2006–2009.
3. It is described as the “Bible” of administrative reform.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Commission submitted 15 reports during 2006–2009 and is described as the “Bible” of administrative reform.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical and descriptive statement before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Second Administrative Reforms Commission - chairman, reports

accepted.s: Which one of the following reports of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission was titled “Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance”?
accepted.x: The First Report was titled “Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance.”
accepted.tq: Match the report number with its distinctive title.
accepted.sec: Second Administrative Reforms Commission - chairman, reports

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a recommendation associated with the Second Administrative Reforms Commission?
o: Lateral entry at the Joint Secretary level
Abolition of right to public services laws
accepted.x: The Commission recommended right to public services laws, not their abolition. It also supported lateral entry, performance-based appraisal and rotational postings.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a recorded recommendation.
accepted.sec: Second Administrative Reforms Commission - chairman, reports

accepted.s: The committee associated with recruitment and selection and the introduction of the three-stage Civil Services Examination from 1979 was:
accepted.x: The D.S. Kothari Committee, constituted in 1976, dealt with recruitment and selection, and its recommendations led to the three-stage CSE from 1979.
accepted.tq: Link the reform focus and implementation year to the correct committee.
accepted.sec: Committees on civil service reform - year and focus

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Satish Chandra Committee — 1989 — Review of CSE, essay paper and greater weight to interview
2. Y.K. Alagh Committee — 2000–01 — Review of the CSE scheme
3. P.C. Hota Committee — 2004 — Domain expertise, lateral entry and appraisal
4. B.S. Baswan Committee — 2016 — CSE eligibility, age limit, attempts and syllabus
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These committees examined the stated aspects of civil service recruitment and reform in the indicated years.
accepted.tq: Verify both the year and the focus in each committee pair.
accepted.sec: Committees on civil service reform - year and focus

accepted.s: The committee set up by the UPSC in July 2000 to review the Civil Services Examination scheme was headed by:
accepted.x: Standard sources identify the July 2000 committee set up by the UPSC with Y.K. Alagh. Sukhadeo Thorat is named in a conflicting examination key, but the standard identification is Alagh.
accepted.tq: Resolve a look-alike attribution by focusing on the standard committee-chairman association.
accepted.sec: Committees on civil service reform - year and focus

accepted.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Doctrine of Pleasure in relation to services?
accepted.x: Article 310 embodies the Doctrine of Pleasure.
accepted.tq: Test precise constitutional article mapping.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for services - Articles 308-323

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)

B. Article 311

D. Article 320

List-II (Subject)
1. Functions of Public Service Commissions
2. Safeguards in dismissal and disciplinary proceedings

accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for services - Articles 308-323

accepted.s: A member of a Public Service Commission is proposed to be removed for misbehaviour. Which procedure is constitutionally relevant?
o: Removal by the Chief Minister after consultation with the State Cabinet
An inquiry by the Supreme Court before removal for misbehaviour
Removal by the Governor without any inquiry
Removal by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha after a simple majority vote
accepted.x: Removal for misbehaviour requires an inquiry by the Supreme Court. The appointing authority cannot remove the member through the procedures stated in the other options.
accepted.tq: Apply the constitutional safeguard by asking which authority performs the inquiry.
accepted.sec: Constitutional provisions for services - Articles 308-323

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Max Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy based on legal-rational authority?
o: Personal patronage as the primary basis of appointment
accepted.x: Weber’s ideal-type bureaucracy is based on hierarchy, rules, impersonality, specialisation, merit and written files. Personal patronage is not its defining basis.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that belongs to a contrasting patronage system.
accepted.sec: Bureaucracy - characteristics, typologies, thinkers

accepted.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the types of bureaucracy identified by F. Morstein Marx?
accepted.x: F. Morstein Marx identified guardian, caste, patronage and merit bureaucracies in The Administrative State.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact four-part typology without confusing it with Weber’s authority types.
accepted.sec: Bureaucracy - characteristics, typologies, thinkers

accepted.s:
Indian bureaucracy comprises which of the following groups?
1. All India Services
2. State services
3. Local government employees
4. PSU managers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The stated conception of Indian bureaucracy includes All India Services, State services, local government employees and PSU managers.
accepted.tq: Check whether the broad institutional composition includes all listed levels and organisations.
accepted.sec: Bureaucracy - characteristics, typologies, thinkers

accepted.s: The first Indian to enter the Indian Civil Service was:
accepted.x: Satyendranath Tagore became the first Indian in the Indian Civil Service in 1864.
accepted.tq: Test a landmark name-year association.
accepted.sec: All India Services - services, new AIS, cadre control, tenure and split systems

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Establishment of the Public Service Commission
B. First Indian in the ICS
C. Federal Public Service Commission under the Government of India Act, 1935
D. Establishment of the UPSC
accepted.x: Satyendranath Tagore entered the ICS in 1864, the Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926, the Federal PSC followed under the 1935 Act, and the UPSC was established in 1950.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest landmark first and then place the two PSC stages before 1950.
accepted.sec: All India Services - services, new AIS, cadre control, tenure and split systems

accepted.s:
Which of the following are All India Services mentioned in the constitutional and administrative framework?
1. Indian Administrative Service
2. Indian Police Service
3. Indian Forest Service
4. Indian Revenue Service
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The listed All India Services are IAS, IPS and Indian Forest Service. Indian Revenue Service is not included in the stated list of All India Services.
accepted.tq: Reject the familiar but constitutionally different central service from the AIS list.
accepted.sec: All India Services - services, new AIS, cadre control, tenure and split systems

accepted.s:

accepted.s: The tenure system under the Central Staffing Scheme refers to:
o: Permanent transfer of every State officer to the Union Government
A fixed term of service at the Centre followed by return to the State cadre
Rotation only among district offices within a State
Appointment of Central officers exclusively to local governments
accepted.x: Under the tenure system, State-cadre officers serve a fixed term at the Centre and then return to their State cadre.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a fixed central deputation followed by return from permanent transfer.
accepted.sec: All India Services - services, new AIS, cadre control, tenure and split systems

accepted.s: The split system in civil administration refers to the separation of:
o: Policy formulation in the Secretariat from implementation through field agencies
accepted.x: The split system separates policy functions performed by the Secretariat from implementation carried out by field agencies.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between policy and implementation functions.
accepted.sec: All India Services - services, new AIS, cadre control, tenure and split systems

accepted.s: Civil Services Day is observed on 21 April because on 21 April 1947:
o: The Federal Public Service Commission was renamed UPSC
Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House, Delhi
The first All India Service was created
The UPSC was established in New Delhi
accepted.x: On 21 April 1947, Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers at Metcalfe House in Delhi and described civil servants as the “steel frame of India.”
accepted.tq: Link the observance date to its historical origin and speaker.
accepted.sec: Civil Services Day - date and origin

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 17th Civil Services Day:
1. It was held on 21 April 2025.
2. It was held at Vigyan Bhawan.
3. Its theme was “Viksit Bharat - Holistic Development of India with focus on Saturation Approach”.
4. Civil Services Day was not held in 2024 because of elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 17th Civil Services Day took place at Vigyan Bhawan on 21 April 2025 with the stated theme, after the event was not held in 2024 because of elections.
accepted.tq: Combine date, venue, theme and exception-year details in one factual check.
accepted.sec: Civil Services Day - date and origin

accepted.s: How many Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration 2024 were recorded in connection with the Civil Services Day information?
accepted.x: The number recorded was 16 Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration 2024.
accepted.tq: Test the exact award count using closely spaced numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Civil Services Day - date and origin

accepted.s: Which rules require political neutrality and integrity from the concerned civil servants?
o: Civil Services Examination Rules, 1968 and Election Rules, 1964
All India Services Act, 1935 and CCS Rules, 1947
accepted.x: The AIS (Conduct) Rules, 1968 and CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 require political neutrality and integrity.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between conduct rules and recruitment or constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: Civil service neutrality and anonymity - conduct rules, debates

accepted.s: Under which provision was an Andhra Pradesh section officer dismissed for campaigning in the 2024 elections?
o: Rule 9 of the AP Civil Services (CCA) Rules, 1991
Rule 43 of the AP Panchayat Raj Act
accepted.x: The section officer was dismissed under Rule 9 of the Andhra Pradesh Civil Services (CCA) Rules, 1991, through G.O. Ms. No. 43 dated 20 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the disciplinary action with the precise rule and State framework.
accepted.sec: Civil service neutrality and anonymity - conduct rules, debates

accepted.s: Which event led to renewed debate on the limits of political neutrality of government employees in Chhattisgarh in April 2026?
o: A Supreme Court order abolishing conduct rules
A permanent ban on all employee associations by Parliament
A circular requiring employees to join a political party
A circular barring employees from membership of any political party or organisation, later withdrawn
accepted.x: Chhattisgarh issued a circular barring employees from membership of any political party or organisation and quickly withdrew it, reopening the neutrality debate.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy action and its subsequent withdrawal rather than accepting an absolute ban as continuing law.
accepted.sec: Civil service neutrality and anonymity - conduct rules, debates

accepted.s:
Which measures are associated with insulating civil servants from undue political pressure?
1. Fixed tenure
2. Civil Services Boards
3. Recommendations in the T.S.R. Subramanian case
4. Recommendations of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Fixed tenure and Civil Services Boards were associated with the T.S.R. Subramanian case and the Second Administrative Reforms Commission in the context of insulating civil servants.
accepted.tq: Recognise the common institutional safeguards across judicial and administrative reform recommendations.
accepted.sec: Civil service neutrality and anonymity - conduct rules, debates

accepted.s: Which statement best represents the contemporary generalist–specialist debate in civil services?
o: Generalist administration has no relevance in nation-building and must be abolished.
Domain expertise is unnecessary where general administrative experience exists.
Generalist design served nation-building, while there is now a case for dedicated scientific cadres and separate scientific service rules.
Specialists should be excluded from all policy-making positions.
accepted.x: The generalist design is recognised as having served nation-building, but the contemporary debate supports dedicated scientific cadres and separate scientific service rules in appropriate fields.
accepted.tq: Balance the historical contribution of generalists against the current case for specialisation.
accepted.sec: Generalist vs specialist debate - lateral entry, domain expertise

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the position on lateral entry into civil services?
o: It is restricted to entry-level clerical posts.
It replaces the Civil Services Examination for all services.
It was opposed by both the Second ARC and the Hota Committee.
It was supported by the Second ARC and the Hota Committee; a UPSC-led, merit-based process has been suggested for domain experts.
accepted.x: Both the Second Administrative Reforms Commission and the P.C. Hota Committee supported lateral entry. A UPSC-led, merit-based process has been suggested for domain experts.
accepted.tq: Compare the positions of two reform bodies and separate lateral entry from total replacement of the CSE.
accepted.sec: Generalist vs specialist debate - lateral entry, domain expertise
